old: You need an MBBS degree from a recognized institution, completed 1-year compulsory rotating internship, and valid NMC/State Medical Council registration. Your NEET PG score must meet the qualifying cutoff (50th percentile for General/EWS category).
new: An MBBS degree recognised by NMC, the internship complete by 30 September 2026 (MCC's cut-off this year), and permanent or provisional registration with NMC or a State Medical Council — provisional only while the internship is on. Your NEET PG score must clear the qualifying percentile NBEMS notifies each year: for 2026, the 50th for General and EWS, the 45th for General PwBD and the 40th for SC, ST and OBC.

old: Yes. If you are allotted a seat in Round 1, you can choose to “float” (retain current seat while participating in next round for a better option) or “resign” (give up current seat). Our experts provide round-by-round upgrade strategies based on real-time vacancy analysis.
new: Yes. After the round 1 result you choose Freeze (join the seat in person, no upgrade) or Float (documents verified online, and you stay in for an upgrade in round 2). A round 1 seat can also be left without losing the security deposit. From round 2, a seat you do not join costs the deposit, and once you join a round 3 seat you can neither resign it nor upgrade from it. Our counsellors plan the call with you round by round.

old: Missing any deadline — registration, choice filling, fee payment, or reporting — typically results in forfeiture of your seat and security deposit. There is usually no appeal process. This is why our deadline management service is critical.
new: It depends on the step. Miss registration or choice filling and you sit that round out. Miss reporting and you lose the seat: in round 1 the security deposit is kept; from round 2 an unjoined seat also costs the deposit, and not joining a round 3 seat takes you out of every further MCC round. MCC does not extend joining dates, which is why we track every deadline with you.

old: NRI quota refers to seats reserved in medical colleges for Non-Resident Indians (NRIs), Person of Indian Origin (PIO), Overseas Citizens of India (OCI), and foreign nationals. Typically, 15% of seats in private and deemed universities are allocated under the NRI/Management quota.
new: Seats set aside for Non-Resident Indians and candidates an NRI relative sponsors, OCI and PIO cardholders and foreign nationals. In deemed universities MCC allots 15% of the seats as NRI seats; in private colleges each state decides whether there is an NRI quota and how big it is.

old: No, not all medical colleges offer NRI quota seats. Most private medical colleges, deemed universities, and some government medical colleges have NRI quota seats. The availability and number of seats vary by institution and are typically regulated by respective state authorities.
new: No. MCC's NRI seats are in the deemed universities; in private colleges each state's rules decide whether a college keeps NRI seats and how many. A state's NRI seat follows that state's own information bulletin, so check the bulletin of every counselling you register for.

old: Yes, many institutions accept NRI-sponsored candidates. The sponsor must be a blood relative (parent, sibling, or specific cousins/uncles/aunts). Relationship requirements vary by institution.
new: Yes, within MCC's rule (from the Supreme Court's Anshul Tomar case): a parent or a real brother or sister who is an NRI; or your nearest NRI relation — a real uncle or aunt on either side, a grandparent or a first cousin — who has looked after you as your guardian, with evidence and an affidavit, and who sponsors the whole course fee. State counsellings set their own rules.

old: Common documents include a valid passport with visa stamps, overseas address proof, employment proof, NRI bank statements, and tax documents from the foreign country.
new: For MCC: an NRI certificate from the Indian embassy or consulate, your valid passport, a notarised affidavit by the NRI sponsor to pay the whole course fee and living costs backed by an NRE passbook, and the relationship verified by a revenue officer such as a Tehsildar — plus your Class 10 and 12 certificates and the NEET score card. The full list, category by category, is on our NRI documents page.
